_note: The real cut of the Ironclad demo, 4 Nov 2026 (published as https://youtu.be/8QMsMO8Dx6E; it fixes the attacks clip, which started 2.3 s early on an idle screen). Cut points and cues come from reading the raw takes frame by frame. Each clip starts about a second before its first event and ends at least three seconds after its last output. Every line has an 'at': seconds into its clip where the event it describes appears, so the voice never runs ahead of the screen. A line that would overlap the one before waits for it; a scene whose voice outlasts its footage holds the last frame.

lines.text: Ironclad gives an AI agent a Zcash wallet it can't overspend.
The key is split three ways, and a co-signer only signs payments inside your rules.
The agent holds one share, and the co-signer holds another.
Two shares make a signature, and the agent only ever has one.
These are the rules, held by the co-signer on the server.
At most 0.2 TAZ a payment, 0.5 a day, and only our Bitrefill counter can be paid.
The co-signer daemon waits with its share.
Now the agent buys a phone top-up.
It builds a shielded payment with the order in the encrypted memo, and syncs over Tor.
Then it asks the co-signer, which checks the payment itself against the rules.
It fits, so the co-signer adds its share, and the payment goes out over Tor.
The counter waits for the block.
Then it buys Bitrefill's test top-up through the live API, and sends a shielded receipt back.
Now say the agent is compromised, and told to send the treasury to an attacker.
It builds that payment just the same.
The co-signer refuses. That address isn't on the list, so no signature exists.
Next it tries 0.25 TAZ to the right address, over the 0.2 cap.
What the prompt said doesn't matter here. The co-signer reads the transaction itself.
Refused again, at the key.
Every decision goes into a hash-chained ledger the owner can audit.
Anyone can check the purchase on Zcash testnet.
The chain shows the block it was mined in. It doesn't show who paid, who was paid, or how much.
The public site shows the same ledger live, with the same keys to try.
Ironclad is open source, and built on frost-zec. Thanks for watching.
